speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is to align energy efficiency standards across sectors, ease regulatory compliance for businesses and improve industrial energy efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The short payback period of 1.5 years also makes installing energy-efficient chilled water systems more cost-effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked how we can support households amid rising utilities costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Climate Friendly Households Programme (CFHP) will help support households to improve resource efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last year, CFHP was enhanced to provide all HDB households in Singapore with $300 worth of Climate Vouchers for purchases from among 10 types of resource-efficient household products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Approximately $88 million of climate vouchers have been utilised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The top three household appliances purchased were direct current fans, refrigerators and washing machines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This translates to annual energy savings that can power 19,000 4-rooms HDB flats and annual water savings equivalent to 900 Olympic-sized swimming pools, or about $31 million in annual utility savings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also expand the enhanced CFHP to include Singapore Citizen households living in private residential properties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This means that each eligible household will, in total, receive $400 of Climate Vouchers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These enhancements will be available from 15 April 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To support our heartland entrepreneurs, MSE has onboarded about 170 retailers, of which, 130 are heartland retailers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Climate Vouchers can be used at over 520 outlets to provide greater accessibility to households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our net-zero targets necessitate the promotion of sustainable consumption and production practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This requires us to reduce resource consumption, reuse where possible, before recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Mr Eric Chua asked how we can promote the 3Rs as a way of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Jean See asked for an update on our measures to manage key waste streams, including packaging waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have made significant strides in facilitating waste reduction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our domestic waste generated per capita, and non-domestic waste generated per dollar GDP decreased by more than 15% and 30% respectively over the past decade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This indicates that households and businesses have taken positive steps to reduce, reuse and recycle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our overall recycling rate remained largely steady at around 60% between 2013 and 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There was a sharp decline during the COVID-19 period and was at 52% in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The recent decline in recycling rate is largely driven by structural factors, such as transport costs, market volatility for recyclables like paper, and foreign government restrictions on the trade in recyclables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These are challenges we must contend with as we work towards closing our resource loop.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will study how we can work together with and support the recycling industry to increase the recycling rate of our key waste streams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One key measure to reduce waste generation and improve recycling is Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), which helps to aggregate clean streams of recyclables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: An upcoming EPR scheme is the beverage container return scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NEA has issued the producer responsibility scheme operator licence to BCRS Ltd, a not-for-profit company formed by a consortium of beverage producers comprising Coca-Cola, F&N Foods and Pokka.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Steady progress is being made to this end.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: BCRS Ltd has called for proposals for the scheme’s IT system, counting and sorting system and the return point network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They have also appointed two small producer representatives to their board of directors to represent smaller producers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: BCRS Ltd will set up more than 1,000 conveniently placed return points to facilitate our recycling journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Alongside EPR schemes, companies are also required to submit plans to reduce packaging use, promote reusables and facilitate collection of packaging for reuse or recycling as part of their Mandatory Packaging Reporting (MPR) submissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MPR seeks to raise companies’ awareness of the packaging waste that they generate and spur them to take concrete steps to reduce it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Companies have taken heed of this call to action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In 2024, NEA supported the launch of an Alliance for Action (AfA) on Packaging Waste Reduction for the e-commerce sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Led by Singapore Manufacturing Federation and Singapore Post, the AfA comprised 14 members across the e-commerce supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The AfA estimates that, in Singapore, about 186,000 parcels were delivered per day in 2023, generating as much as 15,900 tonnes of mailing packaging in that year alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Guidelines provide a comprehensive list of 3R solutions for common packaging types, such as cardboard boxes, mailers and fillers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These solutions are rated based on effort required, cost and environmental impact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Companies can adopt solutions that best suit their needs to achieve cost savings and minimise environmental impact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We hope that more e-commerce businesses will make good use of these guidelines, which can be downloaded from the Packaging Partnership Programme website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On Mr Gerald Giam’s suggestion to provide free or low-cost drinking water to reduce plastic waste, tap water in Singapore is safe for drinking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Water dispensers are also readily available at hawker centres and in common areas, such as parks, bus interchanges and terminals, where one can simply fill up with a reusable which we have been promoting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As we press on towards a sustainable and circular economy, we must also continue to strengthen our water resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Most Members would be familiar with our water supply infrastructure, like our desalination plants, reservoirs and waterways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Fewer might be familiar with the essential role that our used water infrastructure plays in supporting our water supply needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: With rising water demand, more used water will be generated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: So, in tandem, we have to expand our used water conveyance and treatment capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To address the need for more used water conveyance capacity, PUB has been expanding the Deep Tunnel Sewerage System (DTSS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The DTSS is an underground superhighway that will convey used water by gravity to three centralised water reclamation plants located at Changi, Tuas and Kranji.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The first phase of the DTSS (DTSS 1) was completed in 2008 and serves the northern and eastern regions of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The second phase of the DTSS (DTSS 2), which is under construction, will serve the western region of Singapore and will be operational by 2027.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In tandem, we have integrated our used water treatment and NEWater production and are expanding their capacities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Tuas Water Reclamation Plant and Tuas NEWater factories are on track to be completed in phases from 2027.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The new Kranji Water Reclamation Plant and Kranji NEWater factory are targeted to be completed by the mid-2030s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Changi Water Reclamation Plant will also be expanded by the mid-2030s, and the construction of the third Changi NEWater factory is targeted to be completed in the next three years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The three-node used water management system at Changi, Tuas and Kranji will play a critical role in helping to meet Singapore’s long-term needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Every drop of used water will be collected, treated and purified in an endless cycle, so that we make the best use of our limited resource.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Indeed, let this be our calling: zero waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Chairman, in conclusion, our sustainability requires collective effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Advancing green initiatives, improving energy efficiency and promoting resource resilience will put us on track to achieve our climate ambitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These can arise from disease outbreaks, climate change and geopolitical tensions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In safeguarding our food resilience, diversifying our import sources remains our core strategy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When accrediting food imports, SFA takes a risk-based approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While products with low food safety risks do not require accreditation, SFA accredits higher-risk food products, like meat and egg products, in line with international practice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This expands our import product range and improves business efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But our food resilience cannot and does not hinge on one single strategy; it requires a multi-pronged approach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, "Our Sustainability, Our Resilience, Our Everyday" represents MSE’s unwavering commitment to a clean, green and resilient Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the last six decades, we have made significant progress in ensuring high levels of public health as our way of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To reinforce good hygiene practices for collective well-being, MSE designated 2024 as the Year of Public Hygiene.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will update on our efforts in addressing persistent challenges, such as littering hotspots, rat infestations and public toilet cleanliness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our community is generally civic-minded, but littering remains a concern due to the inconsiderate actions of some people.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about NEA’s efforts in improving cleanliness at littering hotspots.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Thanks to the collective efforts by premises owners, cleaners and members of the public, Causeway Point, Chinatown Complex, Jurong Point and Vista Point are on track to be exited from the list of littering hotspots.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA will continue to tackle the remaining hotspots through appropriate interventions, including public education and enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On high-rise littering, we share Ms Hany Soh’s concern.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: High-rise littering is a serious offence, as it poses a danger to the public and dirties the environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To address it, NEA has leveraged camera surveillance and the presumption clause in the Environmental Public Health Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Hany Soh and Ms Nadia Samdin will be glad to hear that data analytics have allowed NEA to prioritise camera deployments and shorten the investigation process, leading to more timely enforcement actions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In the coming months, NEA will also extend camera surveillance duration from the current 14 days, to up to 28 days, to improve the chances of capturing high-rise littering incidents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Reducing the incidence of vector-borne diseases remains a priority.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Hany Soh and Mr Eric Chua asked about MSE’s pest control efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In 2024, NEA worked with stakeholders on upstream measures to improve their housekeeping and refuse management.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is to deny rats access to habitats and food sources, especially food waste.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, NEA also provided training and practical resources, such as guidelines and cleaning and maintenance sample contract specifications, to help stakeholders manage rat-related issues holistically.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin may be interested to hear that NEA also uses technology to enhance rat surveillance for more targeted interventions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One example is the implementation of thermal imaging technology which complements existing ones, such as infrared cameras, with clearer data on potential food sources for rats, their congregation areas and the pathways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As rats multiply quickly, keeping their population low requires sustained efforts from everyone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To this end, NEA shares surveillance data with stakeholders, such as Town Councils and premises owners, so that they can implement measures to prevent rat infestations, including denying the access to habitats and food sources.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Enforcement will continue to play a key role.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: From 1 April 2025, NEA will tighten its enforcement regime, including for poor refuse management and housekeeping.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Shifting to mosquito control, community vigilance and innovations like Project Wolbachia have helped us avoid major dengue surges in 2023 and 2024.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Going forward, we will scale up Project Wolbachia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The expansion to Jurong East since February and Jurong West in April this year will increase Project Wolbachia’s coverage to 580,000 households.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I assure Mr Gan Thiam Poh that we will announce details on future expansion when ready.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA will also be conducting pilots to understand the technology’s ability to disrupt dengue clusters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To address Mr Eric Chua's residents’ concerns on Wolbachia-Aedes releases, NEA will respond promptly to feedback to assure residents on the temporary nature of the increased mosquito presence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over time, with the community’s support, we can maintain low mosquito population, which will lead to fewer releases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Even as we leverage technology, stakeholders and residents must continue to take action to prevent mosquito breeding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Community vigilance is needed to keep dengue at bay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Several Members have asked about public toilet cleanliness and the Public Toilets Taskforce’s recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Taskforce focused on public toilets that consistently fare poorly in cleanliness surveys, including that conducted by Singapore Management University students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: After almost a year of engagement and discussions, the Taskforce, which I co-chaired with Mr Andrew Khng, the Chairman of Public Hygiene Council, submitted our recommendations to Minister Grace Fu recently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Minister has shared that MSE endorses the Taskforce’s recommendations, namely, to "Build Well, Clean Well, and Use Well".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: First, to achieve cleaner public toilets, good toilet design is important as it facilitates easy maintenance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To this end, we welcome the Taskforce’s list of recommended toilet design features.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Deep cleaning and providing better training support for cleaners are also critical to improve toilet cleanliness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Taskforce also recommended grants to support coffee shop operators in toilet upgrading or deep cleaning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, coffee shops are privately-operated commercial premises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, they keep their toilets accessible to patrons and non-patrons, providing a public service to the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is particularly important in an ageing population, as seniors may have more difficulties in managing bladder and bowel control.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Instead of building public toilets in the community, the Government could tap on the Singapore culture of coffee shops being natural gathering points for residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: More information will be provided to coffee shops to help them understand the recommended design features, the adoption of which is a criterion for the renovation grant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Successful grant applicants will also receive complimentary onsite training for their in-house cleaners to improve their cleaning effectiveness and efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Toilet users and community volunteers can also contribute to cleaner toilets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To cultivate shared responsibility for public toilet cleanliness, we endorse the Taskforce’s recommendation to refresh the Happy Toilet Programme by the Restroom Association Singapore and expand the Neighbourhood Toilets Community Group programme by the Public Hygiene Council.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Leveraging technology, such as feedback systems, can facilitate timely feedback, and contribute to public toilet cleanliness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With the Taskforce’s support, the ReportLah! solution is now trialled at over 10 coffee shops in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Furthermore, we will continue to enforce against errant operators, including suspensions where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I am heartened that premises have taken action to rectify lapses and encourage them to sustain their efforts to ensure cleaner toilets for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over time, we hope that these measures will break the cycle of dirty coffee shop toilets, so that we all can enjoy better and cleaner toilets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In Mandarin):   Gathering and chatting with neighbours at coffee shops is part of our Singapore culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Anyone, even if not a customer of the coffee shop, can still use the toilets there.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is a public service that coffee shop operators provide to the community, and it is especially important in an ageing society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Therefore, the Government will provide grants to coffee shop operators to encourage them to adopt good toilet designs and conduct regular deep cleaning of toilets, enabling the public to access better and cleaner toilets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Cleaners from successful applicants will also receive free on-site cleaning training to help improve toilet cleanliness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA will provide more details about the grants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Improving public toilet hygiene requires continuous effort from both toilet operators and users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Clean toilets benefit everyone. : Finally, Mr Louis Ng asked about legislating a smoking ban at windows and balconies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Expanding smoking restrictions to cover private homes and spaces must be carefully considered as this infringes the privacy of people in their own homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Even with legislation, we need enforcement for restrictions to be effective.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The challenge is that current technologies do not allow the detection of smoking activities at home without infringing privacy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, I urge smokers to exercise social responsibility to minimise the impact that smoking has on the well-being of others, including their neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I know that some smokers choose to smoke at windows and balconies so that their family members are not exposed to second-hand tobacco smoke.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As the Chinese saying goes, "己所不欲勿施于人", which means "extending to others the courtesy you would like in return", I urge smokers to exercise the same consideration to their neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Close your door and windows if you do smoke at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Otherwise, go downstairs and smoke away from your block in a non-smoking prohibited area, such as open spaces and unsheltered carparks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We can work together as a community to engender a more gracious society as we shape social norms on acceptable smoking behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MSE and NEA will work together with stakeholders to develop ground-up solutions and promote socially responsible behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, the Year of Public Hygiene has empowered the community and stakeholders to explore new ways to achieve better public health outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To consolidate these gains, NEA will introduce a new concept of operations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Called "Cleaner Neighbourhood", this aims to strengthen community involvement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA will adopt an integrated operations and outreach approach to tackle hotspots with cleanliness, refuse management and congregation problems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA will also seek to address the issues upstream, with broader community involvement and greater use of technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will include upskilling NEA officers to be more effective at managing multifaceted public hygiene issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Surveillance data will also be shared with stakeholders, such as Town Councils, trade premises and dormitory operators, to better support their preventive and corrective measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: A new initiative, called the Community Action for Cleanliness, will complement operations at identified hotspots with engagement of local stakeholders to address community pain points more holistically and effectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To Ms Poh Li San and Ms Nadia Samdin's queries, technology is also being leveraged in other parts of the MSE Family to improve productivity and deliver better public services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The technology provides for speedier and more accurate detection of defects, allowing PUB to respond in a timelier manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In 2022, SFA introduced a mobile lab for onsite testing during food safety incidents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This allows SFA to quickly identify potential food safety risks onsite at large-scale events.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, we received strong support from the community in the Year of Public Hygiene.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over 1,700 activities were co-organised by NEA and community partners to promote good cleanliness and hygiene practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Many partners will continue these initiatives in 2025 and beyond.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, the Chinese Development Assistance Council (CDAC), ran a campaign titled "Clean Districts, Amazing Communities" in partnership with NEA, seven Town Councils, and susGain.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over 120 litter-picking activities and 620 zero-waste activities were completed by the various CDAC centres islandwide from June to September 2024.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Post-campaign, CDAC continued its partnership with NEA to promote a sustainable lifestyle among its beneficiaries and volunteers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum asked about community engagement and action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This year, as we celebrate SG60, we will provide more opportunities for everyone to co-create a sustainable Singapore together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since the launch of the SG Eco Fund in 2020, more than $13 million in funding has empowered over 300 individuals, groups and organisations to initiate projects that involve the community to advance environmental sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I encourage interested parties to step forward in the spirit of SG60 and the SG Eco Fund, to play your special part and make a difference together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Connecting like-minded partners, including our youths, strengthen our collective ability to tackle sustainability and climate change issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last year, I talked about how the #GreenHacks Youth Panel lets interested youths contribute to policymaking and other green efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This year, we will forge on with the Climate Youth Development Programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the last two years, we have equipped 80 youths with relevant knowledge so that they can contribute purposefully towards sustainability and climate change issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Some of them have since amplified their learnings to other stakeholders and started ground-up projects to encourage community action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are inspired by our youths' dedication to a cleaner, greener Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through our initiatives, we will partner and enable them to be effective pathfinders of our present and their future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Fellow Singaporeans can play a part as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Join our Coastal Conversations to shape the future of our coastal areas, participate in the annual Go Green SG from 16 May to 29 June 2025 and practise green habits to support our sustainable cooling movement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: There is a lot more that we can do together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MSE will continue to partner all segments of society to make a difference.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Together, we can achieve sustainability, resilience and a better everyday life for all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But we do have a law making it illegal to be naked at home if it is in public view, and we can enforce that.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, why can NEA or MSE not then enforce this ban on smoking in your home?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, I think many of us receive complaints from our residents about second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, if this resident goes through the entire journey and it does not work, can I ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary what help can NEA offer to these residents who are really suffering from second-hand smoke?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Chairman, I can always count on Mr Chua to continue his crusade.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Smoking, as I said, our current surveillance technology does not allow us to do that.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, if we have a law, the public or complainants will expect the Government to take action, and we do not have credible, efficient technologies that we are able to do that.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In fact, Mr Louis Ng will also disappoint his residents because we are not able to take enforcement action.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I do not like to compare smoking with going around naked at home.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I suppose, for streakers at home, probably it is their neighbours who may complain or will try to take pictures and get the authorities to take action.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I think it is not entirely apple-for-apple kind of comparison.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Would the Ministry consider encouraging or requiring all F&B outlets to provide plain drinking water at free or low cost to customers, instead of charging $2 or more for bottled water, which often comes in a plastic single-use bottle?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: This will promote healthier beverage choices by making plain water more accessible and reduce consumption of sugary drinks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I must say that I am glad that Mr Louis Ng has got a fresh perspective from my colleague.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But with regard to Mr Gerald Giam's question, as I have said, tap water is safe for drinking in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think PUB has reiterated many times and we do have lots of water dispenser, water points, water cooler at the hawker centres, at regional parks, at the bus terminals and interchanges.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, BCA's Green Mark scheme actually awards points to developers or building owners who provide water coolers or water points within their premises, within their building, whether it is in a common area near the toilets and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And even BCA, the Health Promotion Board had a Green Mark for healthier workplaces, also awards points to office premises which put water points within the offices.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: You just need to bring your reusable, which we have been promoting through our "Say YES to Waste Less" campaign, for many many years, and then you can actually fill up and get your water.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think it is up to the F&B businesses to decide how to charge and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There is a lot of competition, so they will take that into account.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And there is a cost to serving the water, the table water, as well as to wash the glasses and so on that it is served in.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we will need to allow them to decide how they are going to provide the service to their customers and whether they will charge or not.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But regardless, the reality is that water is easily accessible from various drinking points.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: The first is to the Minister in relation to her announcement of HUP 2.0.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I understand that there is a long-term plan for existing hawker centres to be transformed.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: In this regard, can I enquire what are the factors which will be taken into consideration in prioritising which estates' hawker centres will be upgraded first?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: The second and third clarifications are to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: The first is in relation to high-rise littering issues.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I understand from Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey that there are plans to place surveillance cameras for a longer period of time, up to 28 days.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: While I appreciate this effort, but based on our residents' feedback, more often than not, it is that surveillance cameras, while they serve a good purpose in enforcement, actually, the better benefits of them actually pertain to deterrence.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: So, I urge the Ministry to consider whether we can explore – rather than a specific duration of 28 days – whether we can have it on a permanent basis.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: It is just like speed cameras, for instance, in the hope that such issues will not recur after the specified period where the cameras have been removed.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: The third point is on the public toilets.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: It has been announced that MSE will set aside some grants for coffee shops' renovations and deep cleaning.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: In this regard, can we actually explore to extend this grant to other toilets that are used by the public as well, outside of coffee shops, for example, those that are at the neighbourhood centres, those that are at the Community Clubs that are actually used by the public as well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Are they in need of a new centre?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Is there a need for consideration or consolidation?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The third one is really to expand further and see whether what are the needs in the surrounding area as well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think the fourth factor would be to really have a very engaged session with our land agencies, such as HDB, URA, to look at the overall master planning of the towns and of the land around these centres.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: She would be aware that for the surveillance cameras to catch high-rise littering, in fact, we have already increased the number of deployments and each of these requires the equipment, the set-up and the checking as well as the analysis of the footages.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The reason why we are extending the deployment period is because these areas tend to be a problem of recalcitrant litterbugs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We hope that with 28 days, four weeks, they will be caught, during this period.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: And when they are caught, they will be subject to penalties.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: If I am not wrong, they will be issued Court orders; you need to go to Court.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, the penalties and the punishment, we hope they will teach them a lesson, that they will change this habit forever.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As we know, there are so many different HDB blocks in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It will not be possible to deploy such surveillance systems on a permanent basis.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: If we dilute our resources to cover other public toilets, then I think the impact will not be significant and it will not address the issue that we are facing at hand.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, I hope that we will have the support to roll this out and get the onboarding of coffee shop operators as well as the cooperation of users and other stakeholders so that we can have cleaner public toilets at coffee shops.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But this is a photo from an NEA camera, showing someone smoking at their window and there is actually quite a number of photos.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The current cameras that we use to catch the litterbugs can catch someone smoking at the windows.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, there really is not an excuse to say that there is no technology.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But there is and we can use that again to legislate and help to protect people from second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Yes, for surveillance cameras to catch high-rise littering, the cameras are typically deployed at the ground level with the camera projected upwards, to try to catch the littering act.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, by counting the floors and which window, which level, the littering act is caught and we are able to take enforcement action.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In those pictures that Mr Louis Ng has shown, those are in rare cases or exceptional places where we are not able to mount cameras on the ground, because by pointing a camera into the windows of a home for suspected littering offences, it really goes into the privacy of the house owner.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We do not think it is something that our residents would appreciate because it could be a suspect household.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It need not be a confirmed smoker causing the nuisance to neighbours.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, it is about this privacy invasion that we are not sure that we should roll it out as a way to catch smoking at windows and balconies.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I really have not received a reply on this from the Ministry.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Chairman, I would like to maybe ask the Member to give me the background, because I think he is referring to a very specific case which I am afraid I am not very familiar with.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is a specific case of a bakery with a ventilation problem that affects the neighbours.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Perhaps, the Member can describe the problem to me again, please, Sir, through you.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I just want to get a better clarification on the issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, I have written to the relevant agencies, and the last round I wrote was to SFA.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I do not think that this is a very major problem on the ground.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I do not hear many such feedback coming from Members.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I will very much appreciate if the Member could file a Parliamentary Question (PQ), so that we can give a fuller reply.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But I will come back with a fuller reply to the Member's PQ.

speaker: The Chairman
text: With that, Mr Louis Ng, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I especially thank Minister Grace Fu, Senior Minister of State Amy Khor, Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng for all their positive responses, except on the issue of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: My persistence on this issue – I have always wanted to say it – is as lingering as second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: That is a persistent problem for so many residents and I hope sooner rather than later, we will really fix this problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I also want to again record my appreciation and thanks, on behalf of all of us, to the staff members at MSE, NEA, SFA and PUB for all their hard work and dedication towards very important causes here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: With that, Sir, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.
